# Success

Authors will be able to describe and check existing tutorials without changing tools. Learners will be able to find materials suited to their goals and experience, while instructors can assess lessons for reuse. Both will be able to compare requirements and check results across engines, with each tutorial's review status clearly stated.

The table compares documented results with grant-end targets. We will update the baseline at grant start to include any completed pilot work.

| Measure | Documented baseline | Grant-end target |
|--------------------------------|-------------------|--------------------------------|
| Adapters with capability reports | 0 demonstrated | 3 initial adapters |
| Tutorials indexed through tutorialverse | 0 demonstrated | 5–10 across supported formats |
| External reviewers of schema, adapters, or tutorials | 0 documented reviews | At least 3 |
| Example tutorials tested in CI | 0 demonstrated | 4, collectively covering all adapters |
| Integration templates | 0 demonstrated | 3–4 |
| Reusable tutorial-validation workflow | 0 demonstrated | At least 1 |

Completion requires version 1.0 of the schema, R package, and registry. We must also publish and test the review and governance policies during the pilot, including procedures for handling stale resources.

Validation will apply only to the checks reported for each engine and environment. During the grant, we will track external submissions and review participation, alongside the effort authors spend supplying missing metadata. After release, outdated check results and broken links will guide maintenance, while package coverage will help us identify gaps in the registry.

Future work could add adapters for other tutorial engines or connect the registry to pkgdown, R-universe, and educational catalogs. Multilingual metadata, richer accessibility checks, and instructor collections remain outside the initial funded scope.
